speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a postmenopausal woman presenting with vaginal bleeding and an adnexal mass; to narrow down the cause, are you currently experiencing pain, fever, or urinary symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old woman. The patient presents with a 2-month history of intermittent postmenopausal bleeding. She denies any recent weight loss, fever, or changes in bladder or bowel habits. No previous history of similar symptoms. She has no history of serious illness and takes no medications regularly.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful; since you deny fever and urinary symptoms, does the bleeding come with pelvic pain, and do you notice any changes in the size of your abdomen? I also need to see the imaging of that adnexal mass to determine if it appears solid or cystic. REQUEST IMAGES: Adnexal_ultrasound

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Intermittent bleeding from the vagina. I also have No recent weight loss, No fever, No changes in bladder or bowel habits.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Endometrial Hyperplasia (with or without atypia) secondary to unopposed estrogen production from a functional ovarian cyst.
While the adnexal mass explains the estrogen source, the primary concern for the bleeding is endometrial pathology; I recommend an endometrial biopsy and repeat ultrasound in 3 months to monitor the ovarian mass.
